intro: A light project board for building software with AI, with you in control.
boardAlt: Pano projects with status counts and work waiting for a test
featuresIntro: Follow the work on the board. Pano tracks agents; it does not run them.
boardText: See your projects and their progress together, including work waiting for your test.
usage: Cards show usage reported by agents. Pano does not measure it or calculate a price.
testingText: Try the scenarios, then approve the result or send it back with a note. Failed scenarios prevent approval.
testAlt: A Test card with instructions and scenarios
historyText: See decisions, checks and changes on each card. Cancelled cards keep their history.
workIntro: Your AI runs the work and Pano keeps track, while you step in at two moments: when you ask and when something needs your test.
backlogText: The PO plans cards with acceptance criteria.
progressText: Agents build and the PO checks their work.
testText: Try the scenarios, then approve or send back.
doneText: Approved work ends here. The card keeps its history.
release: These commands work once the first release is published. Until then:
serve: Run pano serve and open http://localhost:7777. For Docker, just open the address.
connectText: You can run the whole process with the CLI, so MCP is optional. Choose what suits you.
skillsText: Paste this into your AI to set up the Skills:
skillsPrompt: Copy skills/pano and skills/pano-po from https://github.com/Metonya/pano into your skills folder.
manual: Or copy those folders yourself. For Claude Code, use ~/.claude/skills/. If your tool has no Skills support, ask it to read both SKILL.md files.
starter: Then start a conversation with your agent:
owner: I keep one PO agent for planning, and we make the decisions together. Through Skills and CLIs it runs my other agents in Claude, Codex and OpenCode like subagents, so its context stays small. Work is tracked card by card and goes to the model that fits it. When something needs my check, it is assigned to me. If it is not right, I send it back. So I don't get lost while AI runs off on its own.
ownerMore: This is the way of working I set up, and it works for me. So I'm publishing the tool behind it as open source. Install it locally and try it yourself.
mcpText: If your tool supports MCP, your AI may find the board a little easier to use. With Pano running, copy the command for your tool to print its setup.
stepAskText: Say what you want and decide the scope.
sendBackReturn: Sent-back work returns to In Progress.
doneNote: If the project allows it, the PO can verify and close work that doesn't need your quality check.
keepLight: Keep it light: one PO and a few agents are enough. Use your own Skills and change the setup to suit you.
